title: Invariant-Preserving Sub-Allocator Composition in a Rust Custom Buddy Memory Allocation System

abstract: We present a Rust implementation of a custom buddy memory allocator that composes multiple sub-allocators into dynamic memory pools. The design enforces two invariants: (i) no double-free of any block and (ii) contiguous arena preservation across split-merge operations. Allocation and deallocation are shown to run in amortized $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time, where $N$ is the number of blocks. Empirical evaluation on an Intel\textregistered{} Xeon\textregistered{} 6973P-C processor (1 core, 2 logical threads, 7.8~GB RAM, Linux 6.17) reports a mean latency of 598.40 \textmu{}s (Std Dev $\pm$ 42.76 \textmu{}s) and a throughput of 1 671 114 operations per second over 30 benchmark iterations. The results confirm that the invariant-driven composition does not degrade performance relative to a monolithic buddy allocator. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/rust-algorithms/tree/main/algorithms/20261011_150203_custom_buddy_memory_allocation}.
